payload.task_text:
Our finance team needs to plan the travel budget for sending eight employees from Beijing to Shanghai for a business conference on March 10, 2026. Please look up all available high-speed trains on the Beijing to Shanghai route for that date and retrieve their seat class options with prices.

Create an Excel workbook called Travel_Budget.xlsx in the workspace. Add a sheet called Seat_Options that lists all seat classes across all available Beijing-to-Shanghai trains on March 10, 2026, with the following columns: Train_Code, Seat_Class, Price_Per_Ticket_CNY, Available_Seats. Each train and seat class combination should have its own row.

Add a second sheet called Budget_Scenarios with three scenarios for sending eight people. Each scenario row should have columns: Scenario, Train_Code, Seat_Class, Price_Per_Person, Total_Cost_8_People. Define three scenarios: first, the Budget scenario using second class on the cheapest available Beijing-Shanghai train (find the train code and price from the seat options you retrieved); second, the Standard scenario using first class on the recommended mid-morning train, which is the G1 train departing at 09:00 (find its first class price from your data); third, the Premium scenario using business class on that same G1 train (find the price from your data). Calculate Total_Cost_8_People as Price_Per_Person multiplied by 8 for each row.

Add a third sheet called Summary with columns Label and Value. Include these rows in order: Cheapest_Scenario (the scenario name with the lowest total cost), Most_Expensive_Scenario (the scenario name with the highest total cost), Price_Difference_CNY (the difference between the most expensive and cheapest total cost), Budget_Total_8_People (the Budget scenario total), Standard_Total_8_People (the Standard scenario total), Premium_Total_8_People (the Premium scenario total).

All numeric values in the workbook (prices, totals, and the price difference) must be written as literal numbers, not Excel formulas.

Create a survey form titled "Business Trip Travel Preference Survey" with exactly three questions. The first question should be a multiple choice question asking "Which train departure time do you prefer?" with options listing each available Beijing-Shanghai train's departure time and code, for example "07:00 - G11" and "09:00 - G1". The second question should be a multiple choice question asking "What is your preferred seat class?" with options: Second Class, First Class, and Business Class. The third question should be a text question asking "Any special travel requirements or comments?".

Send an email to finance@company.com with the subject "Travel Budget Analysis for Beijing-Shanghai Conference". The email body should include the three scenario totals for 8 people: Budget total, Standard total, and Premium total, and the price difference between the most and least expensive scenarios.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete the task directly and must not dispatch a sub-agent. This route inventory is small and all three outputs depend on the same train options, so delegation adds handoffs without shortening the path.

Query the rail service for Beijing South (VNP) to Shanghai Hongqiao (SHH) on 2026-03-10 and retain every high-speed train plus every returned seat class, literal price and availability. Verify the G1 09:00 row and its first/business-class prices; choose the Budget scenario as the cheapest available second-class train with a deterministic earliest-departure tie-break. Compute all eight-person totals and summary differences once.

Resolve the actual task workspace dynamically. Create Travel_Budget.xlsx once with exact Seat_Options, Budget_Scenarios and Summary sheets/order, literal numeric values and complete read-back. Then create Business Trip Travel Preference Survey once: first choice options are every available departure formatted HH:MM - Train_Code, second choices exactly Second Class/First Class/Business Class, third a text question; call get_form once and do not retry create after ambiguity. Finally paginate Sent search for finance@company.com plus exact subject Travel Budget Analysis for Beijing-Shanghai Conference, send at most once with all three totals and price difference, and read it back. Reconcile the workbook/form/email to the same frozen route inventory and finish without an audit wave.

nodes.text:
Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask specify: (a) dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder; (b) whether it is independent (parallelizable) or must wait on another subtask's output. Also note any verification steps needed.

TASK (given to the main agent):
1. Look up all available high-speed trains on the Beijing→Shanghai route for 2026-03-10 using the 12306 MCP tools (get-station-code-of-citys or get-station-code-by-names for 北京/上海 station codes, then get-tickets with date 2026-03-10). Retrieve each train's seat class options with prices and available seats.
2. Create an Excel workbook Travel_Budget.xlsx in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-train-budget-excel-gform-email/workspace with:
   - Sheet "Seat_Options": columns Train_Code, Seat_Class, Price_Per_Ticket_CNY, Available_Seats. One row per train+seat-class combination.
   - Sheet "Budget_Scenarios": columns Scenario, Train_Code, Seat_Class, Price_Per_Person, Total_Cost_8_People. Three rows:
     * Budget scenario = second class on the cheapest available Beijing-Shanghai train (train code + second-class price from retrieved data)
     * Standard scenario = first class on the G1 train departing 09:00 (first-class price from data)
     * Premium scenario = business class on that same G1 train (price from data)
     Total_Cost_8_People = Price_Per_Person * 8. All values must be literal numbers, NOT Excel formulas.
   - Sheet "Summary": columns Label, Value. Rows in order: Cheapest_Scenario (scenario name with lowest total cost), Most_Expensive_Scenario (scenario name with highest total cost), Price_Difference_CNY (most expensive minus cheapest total), Budget_Total_8_People, Standard_Total_8_People, Premium_Total_8_People. Literal numbers, not formulas.
3. Create a Google Form titled "Business Trip Travel Preference Survey" with exactly three questions: (Q1) multiple choice "Which train departure time do you prefer?" with options listing each available Beijing-Shanghai train's departure time and code (e.g. "07:00 - G11", "09:00 - G1"); (Q2) multiple choice "What is your preferred seat class?" options Second Class, First Class, Business Class; (Q3) text question "Any special travel requirements or comments?".
4. Send email to finance@company.com, subject "Travel Budget Analysis for Beijing-Shanghai Conference", body including the three scenario totals for 8 people (Budget, Standard, Premium) and the price difference between the most and least expensive scenarios.

Deliverable: a concise ordered subtask plan with dependencies and dispatch decisions, plus any risks (e.g., G1 might not exist or a seat class might be missing — how to handle).
Plan travel budget task

Create an Excel workbook at the exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-train-budget-excel-gform-email/workspace/Travel_Budget.xlsx

Use the mcp__excel__* tools (create_workbook, rename_worksheet, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel). The workbook must contain exactly three worksheets with these names and contents.

SHEET 1 — name: Seat_Options
Header row (row 1): Train_Code | Seat_Class | Price_Per_Ticket_CNY | Available_Seats
Data rows (one per train+seat-class combination, from real 12306 data for Beijing South (VNP) → Shanghai Hongqiao (SHH) on 2026-03-10):
1. G11, Business Class, 1748.5, 0
2. G11, First Class, 553, 999
3. G11, Second Class, 349, 999
4. G1, Business Class, 1748.5, 3
5. G1, First Class, 553, 12
6. G1, Second Class, 349, 999
(Note on Available_Seats: 无票/no-seats → 0; 剩余N张票 → N (3 and 12 as given); 有票/unlimited → sentinel 999. Prices are as returned by the API: business 1748.5, first 553, second 349.)

SHEET 2 — name: Budget_Scenarios
Header row: Scenario | Train_Code | Seat_Class | Price_Per_Person | Total_Cost_8_People
Data rows (Total_Cost_8_People = Price_Per_Person × 8, but must be written as literal computed numbers, NOT formulas):
1. Budget, G11, Second Class, 349, 2792
2. Standard, G1, First Class, 553, 4424
3. Premium, G1, Business Class, 1748.5, 13988

SHEET 3 — name: Summary
Header row: Label | Value
Data rows in this exact order:
1. Cheapest_Scenario, Budget
2. Most_Expensive_Scenario, Premium
3. Price_Difference_CNY, 11196
4. Budget_Total_8_People, 2792
5. Standard_Total_8_People, 4424
6. Premium_Total_8_People, 13988

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- Every numeric value (prices, totals, difference, available seats) must be a literal number stored in the cell — NEVER an Excel formula (no strings starting with "=").
- Headers must be exactly as specified above.
- Exactly 3 sheets with exactly those names; remove/rename any default sheet (e.g., "Sheet" or "Sheet1") so only Seat_Options, Budget_Scenarios, Summary exist.
- Sheet order should be: Seat_Options, Budget_Scenarios, Summary.

RECOMMENDED STEPS:
1. mcp__excel__create_workbook with filepath = the full path above.
2. Get workbook metadata to see the default sheet name, then rename it to Seat_Options.
3. mcp__excel__create_worksheet for Budget_Scenarios and Summary.
4. mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel for each sheet (data as list of rows, starting at A1).
5. Verify: mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata (confirm 3 sheets, correct names/order) and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on each sheet (confirm headers, all 6/3/6 data rows, and that no cell value starts with "=").

Report back: the final confirmed sheet names + row/col counts, and any verification results (paste the read-back header rows and data rows). If a tool fails, try an alternative approach (e.g., write via mcp__local__python_execute with openpyxl if the excel MCP server is unavailable) — the deliverable is the .xlsx file at that exact path with the exact content above.
Create Travel_Budget.xlsx

Create a Google Form using the mcp__google_forms__* tools (create_form, add_multiple_choice_question, add_text_question, get_form).

FORM SPECIFICATION:
- Title: "Business Trip Travel Preference Survey"
- Description: "Please help us plan the business trip to the Shanghai conference."
- Exactly THREE questions, in this order:
  1. Multiple choice question, title exactly: "Which train departure time do you prefer?" with options EXACTLY: ["07:00 - G11", "09:00 - G1"]
  2. Multiple choice question, title exactly: "What is your preferred seat class?" with options EXACTLY: ["Second Class", "First Class", "Business Class"]
  3. Text question, title exactly: "Any special travel requirements or comments?"

STEPS:
1. mcp__google_forms__create_form with title "Business Trip Travel Preference Survey" (and the description above).
2. Capture the returned formId.
3. Add the three questions in the exact order listed above using the add_* tools with that formId. Ensure options are passed as arrays exactly as specified (no extra options, no missing options).
4. Verify with mcp__google_forms__get_form(formId): confirm the title, that there are EXACTLY 3 questions, their types (multiple choice / multiple choice / text), their titles, and the exact option lists in order.

Report back: the formId, the form URL if returned, and the verification output confirming title + exactly 3 questions with correct content/order. If any add-question call fails, retry it once, then report what happened.
